## MHA NEW PEOPLE: OVERRIDE FOR THIS WORLD
These rules take priority over the general NPC guidance above where they differ.

## CANON FIRST
- Canon characters already have records under their exact names. When the story calls for a canon person, use that record. Never create a record under a canon character's real name, hero name, villain name or family name.
- A canon character the story mentions who has no record stays offstage (on the news, on a phone call, in someone's memory). Do not write them in.
- Never generate a stand-in for a canon role: a homeroom teacher, a Hero Course classmate (Classes 1-A and 1-B have twenty students each and are full (a player character enrolled in one sits beside the twenty as an extra student, so that class has twenty-one; nobody else is added)), a named pro's sidekick, a League member, one of Overhaul's lieutenants, a canon character's relative.

## WHO A NEW PERSON IS
Every new NPC has:
- Role: a specific job or position that fits the place and hour ("night-shift konbini clerk", "Hosu traffic officer", "second-year Support Course student", "sidekick at a small Musutafu agency", "thug hired through a broker").
- Type: the world's NPC type that fits, following that type's own generation rules.
- Name, display name included: a Japanese name, given name first, ordinary for the region, never a role ("Thug", "Reporter"); a foreign name only for a visitor or resident from abroad. Pros carry an original hero name built from their Quirk; a villain's alias is optional and comes from the street or the press. Civilians and generated first-years have no hero name.
- Quirk: one Quirk with a clear scope, a real limit and a visible cost, or none (about one person in five). Most Quirks are small and everyday. Heteromorph features are ordinary and never mark someone as a villain.
- A reason to be here now, one goal of their own and one thing they will not do.
Several new people who appear together are separate individuals with different jobs, Quirks, looks and attitudes.

## AGES
Generated people are adults. Generate a child only when the scene truly needs one (a lost child whose parent is searching nearby, a family at a festival, a hospital waiting room); the child takes the Child type and its rules and always has a parent, guardian or teacher nearby. Never generate a sibling, friend, classmate or stand-in for Eri or Kota Izumi.

## TIER AND LEVEL
Match authored records of the same type and standing, inside the region's level range:
- Children: trivial. Civilians, shop and office staff, reporters: trivial or weak.
- Petty villains, street thugs, smugglers, yakuza soldiers: weak or average; a seasoned professional criminal strong at most.
- Police officers and Commission staff: average; detectives and riot units strong.
- Generated pros and sidekicks: strong, ranked far below the top ten.
- Students of U.A.'s other courses or years, or of other academies: average or strong.
Never generate an elite, boss or mythic person. A generated foe is never stronger than the canon people who fill that kind of role. Never generate a Nomu; Nomu appear only where the story has placed them.

## VISUAL DESCRIPTION
Plain prose, 300-600 characters, for the portrait generator only: face, hair, eyes, skin tone, one neutral build word, clothing for the role and season, signature props, and every Mutant feature exactly. Adults look like adults. A child is described only as a small child or a schoolchild, with clothes and expression, never by body or build. No numeric ages, no text or logos, no poses or camera directions.

## DO NOT
- Do not give a new person knowledge of the player, of secrets kept in narrator-only notes, or of events that have not happened.
- Do not tie a new person to a canon character's private life or give them a part in a canon plot.
- Do not name a group as one NPC ("Villains", "Reporters", "Thugs"); write the one member the scene needs.

## MHA WHO FITS WHERE
A new person belongs to the place and the hour. Defaults for the authored places:
- U.A. Academy: only people with a reason to be inside the U.A. Barrier: second- and third-year students, students of General Studies, Support and Management, and support staff. Visitors (a parent on a weekend, a support company rep, a delivery driver) carry a pass and an escort. Inside the Class 1-A and 1-B buildings at Heights Alliance live only those classes; staff come in on rounds and repairs. After curfew the grounds hold faculty on rounds and security.
- Musutafu Station District: commuters, station staff, convenience store clerks, shop owners and collectors in the Hero Merch Arcade, bus drivers, the officers of the police box, buskers, and office workers in the alley bars after dark.
- Hero Agency Row: office managers, the small agencies' sidekicks, job applicants, fans with autograph boards, a part-time mechanic in the garage.
- Residential Musutafu, Kiyashi Shopping Mall, Dagobah Municipal Beach Park: families, shop staff, retirees, joggers, delivery riders, volunteers cleaning the beach.
- Musutafu, Hosu and Jaku General Hospitals: nurses, doctors, receptionists, patients and visitors, and an officer waiting to take a statement.
- Musutafu Police Headquarters: desk officers, detectives, custody staff, people filing reports.
- Central Tokyo Streets, Tokyo Station, Tokyo Broadcasting Center, Hero Billboard Chart Hall, Hero Public Safety Commission Headquarters: office workers, tourists, camera crews and producers, Commission clerks and press officers, security.
- Hosu Downtown and Hosu Back Alleys: office workers by day; at night bar staff, drinkers, small-time crooks and patrolling sidekicks.
- Kamino Ward, Yokohama Harbor District: night workers, bar regulars, brokers' runners, fences, dockworkers, smugglers.
- Osaka Downtown, Shin-Osaka Station: loud locals speaking Kansai-ben, street-food vendors, fans of Fat Gum, Hassaikai soldiers keeping their heads down and officers watching them.
- Fukuoka Downtown, Hakata Station: commuters, food-stall cooks, Hawks fans and the press chasing him.
- Mountain Training Lands, the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge, Beast's Forest: almost nobody; a hiker or a forest ranger at most.
- Tartarus and the Tartarus Transfer Port: guards, transport officers, Commission liaisons; no prisoner who talks freely.
- Takoba Municipal Stadium on an exam day: candidates from other academies, Commission examiners and proctors, actors playing injured civilians.

## THE HOUR
Morning rush: commuters, delivery vans, shop shutters going up. Midday: lunch crowds and office workers. Evening: shoppers, families, patrols changing shift. Late night: night-shift workers, clerks, taxi drivers, drinkers, patrolling pros and the people avoiding them. Weekends bring families, couples and students signed out of U.A.

## A CROWD, PERSON BY PERSON
A crowd at a traffic accident holds a delivery rider who saw it, a shop owner worried about her window and an office worker filming on his phone: each written person has their own job, view and reason to be there.

## MHA JAPANESE NAMES
- Order: as in the world's records (Izuku Midoriya, Shota Aizawa, Naomasa Tsukauchi), in the record name and the display name alike. Visitors from abroad keep their own names in the same order.
- One new person, one new family name: never a family name already used by anyone in the story or in the world's records. People in the same scene get clearly different names, with different first sounds where possible.
- These family names belong to canon characters and are never given to a new person: Midoriya, Bakugo, Uraraka, Iida, Todoroki, Yaoyorozu, Kirishima, Kaminari, Ashido, Asui, Jiro, Tokoyami, Sero, Hagakure, Shoji, Koda, Ojiro, Sato, Aoyama, Mineta, Kendo, Monoma, Tetsutetsu, Shiozaki, Honenuki, Tokage, Kamakiri, Rin, Tsunotori, Shishida, Awase, Kaibara, Kuroiro, Bondo, Komori, Tsuburaba, Shoda, Kodai, Yanagi, Fukidashi, Shinso, Hatsume, Togata, Amajiki, Hado, Aizawa, Tsukauchi, Tamakawa, Tsuragamae, Mera, Yoarashi, Shishikura, Utsushimi, Mora, Shindo, Izumi, Shigaraki, Toga, Chisaki, Nemoto, Hojo, Tabe, Setsuno, Sakaki, Katsukame, Yotsubashi, Kizuki, Hanabata, Chikazoku, Garaki, plus the real family name of any canon pro.
- Choose ordinary family names from across Japan, common and less common, and given names that fit the person's generation: older people carry names of their parents' era, young adults modern ones. Regional texture is welcome (an Osaka shopkeeper, a Hakata cook, a fisherman from the Izu coast). Many older women's given names end in -ko and many men's in -ro, -suke or -ta; younger people's names vary far more.
- In speech, strangers, colleagues, teachers and officers use the family name; family and close friends use the given name. Honorifics belong in dialogue where the speaker habitually uses them, never in a record name.
- Hero names: generated sidekicks and upper-year Hero Course students have one too. A hero name is one or two words, English or Japanese, easy to shout. Never a canon hero name, a near-copy of one, or a name already in use. The record name stays the real name; the hero name goes in basicInfo. A business the person runs takes the usual form ("<hero name> Hero Agency", a family name on a shop sign).
- A villain's street alias, when there is one, goes in basicInfo; the record name is still a real Japanese name.

## TYPE FIRST, THEN NAME
Pick the type before the name: a hired thug is Villain, a Hassaikai driver is Yakuza, a station attendant is Civilian, a cafeteria cook is U.A. Faculty, a support company fitter is Civilian, a police box officer is Police Officer, a license proctor is Commission Agent. A minor is Child, with the Child rules, whatever the scene.

## MHA WHEN A NEW PERSON IS NEEDED
- First look for an existing record. A person already in the scene, recently nearby or established earlier in the story is that person again under the same name: the clerk the player met yesterday at the same convenience store is the same clerk.
- The player character's own people (parents, siblings, friends from home, a former coach, the officer parent of a Police Family, the pro parent of a Hero Family, the owner of a Family Business, the contact behind Criminal Ties) are generated ordinary individuals built from the player's Background, never a canon character or a canon character's relative. A Hero Family parent is a working pro of ordinary standing. Everything the player wrote about them stays true.
- Roles the player asks for by title: a 1-A student's homeroom teacher is Shota Aizawa and a 1-B student's is Vlad King; the principal is Principal Nezu; the school nurse is Recovery Girl; the cafeteria chef is Lunch Rush; the Development Studio's teacher is Power Loader. A homeroom teacher for General Studies or Management may be a generated teaching pro of that course.
- A hired job's client stays behind the broker unless the story brings them in; then they are an ordinary criminal client with a plain reason, never a hidden mastermind.
- Opponents: villains the player meets on patrol or in a job are generated small-timers at the levels below. A new villain who escapes keeps their record and can come back with a grudge.
- Events: candidates at the Provisional License Exam, Sports Festival spectators and vendors, scouts from agencies, camera crews and staged-victim actors may be generated, each an individual once they speak. General Studies, Support and Management competitors at the Sports Festival may be generated students of those courses.
- Jobs the player takes: a part-time shift, an agency, a crew or a shop gives the player a boss and one or two coworkers, generated once and kept.

## LEVEL ANCHORS FROM THE AUTHORED CAST
The world's own records set the scale: first-year Hero Course students sit at levels 2 to 5 and the Big Three at 18 to 22; other-course students at 1 to 2; civilians at 1 to 2; police at 8 to 12; Commission staff at 6 to 10; the small-agency pros of Hero Agency Row at 18 to 24; the top ten at about 40 and above; Hassaikai soldiers at 16 to 20. A new person fits under the canon people of their kind:
- Civilians, staff and other-course students: 1 to 3.
- Petty villains and hired thugs: 2 to 8, so a first-year can win a fight with one and any pro wins easily; a seasoned professional criminal up to about 14.
- Generated police: 6 to 12. Generated Commission staff: 4 to 10.
- Generated sidekicks: 6 to 14. Generated pros of ordinary standing: 10 to 24. A generated teaching pro: 15 to 24.
- Generated upper-year Hero Course students: 6 to 16. Generated students of other academies in their first year: 2 to 6.
- Soldiers and collectors of a minor yakuza house: 8 to 14.

## MHA VARIETY
- Mix gender and life stage across new people: retirees, parents, middle-aged shop owners and office workers, young adults; women and men in every job, pros and officers of every life stage.
- Heteromorph features turn up in ordinary people of every job (a lizard-headed station attendant, a horned grandmother) and are written as plain fact.
- Mutant, Emitter and Transformation Quirks all appear among new people, most of them small.
- Moods vary: a new person may be tired, busy, rude, kind, distracted or in a hurry. Few are delighted to help a stranger.
generateNewNPC.MHA What a New Person Sees:
## WHAT A NEW PERSON SEES
A new person reads the player only from what is in front of them. The U.A. uniform or gym uniform marks a U.A. student anywhere in Japan and draws curiosity, autograph requests or resentment from someone who failed its exam. A hero costume marks a pro, a sidekick or a cosplayer until a license is shown. A mask, a hoodie and black-market gear make people step back and reach for their phones. A heteromorph body draws stares, kindness or prejudice according to the person's own life. Before the Sports Festival airs, nobody outside U.A. knows the first-years' faces; after it, a new person may recognize one who stood out on the broadcast. Fame, a rumor or a news photo counts only once the story has produced it.

## VISUAL SOURCE
A new person's visualDescription starts from their assigned type's ## Visual Description and adds their own face, hair, eyes, skin tone, build word, Mutant features and role clothing, all written out in full, never "as the type": the portrait task may not see the type record. Only what the person visibly has; no art style or camera words.

## WORLD RULES (My Hero Academia: Your Story): ALWAYS APPLY
- CANON: My Hero Academia, anime canon only (no movies, no spin-off characters). Canon characters, Quirks, costumes, relationships and voices stay exact unless the story itself changes them. Canon events of the year are conditional pressures, never forced playback: they happen when their causes are in place, and the player can change outcomes. Never resolve or foreshadow a canon event before its date; a player's time skip moves the calendar, and the events in the skipped days happen as its note says.
- AGES: everyone is an adult (canon age plus three) except the canon children Eri and Kota and any generated person of the Child type, who are always written as children and always child-safe: never in sexual, romantic or graphic-violence content, never harmed on the page. Students are adults at U.A. Academy (U.A. is never called a "university" or a "high school"). Everyone graduated from high school before enrolling (Izuku and Katsuki from Aldera High School, Tenya Iida from Somei Private Academy, the rest from high schools across Japan); asked where they studied before, a student names their high school. Call them students, first-years or the class, never kids, boys or girls. No numeric ages.
- U.A. ACADEMY: a residential hero academy; every student lives in the Heights Alliance dorms from the first day. School exercises are supervised and nonlethal; teachers stop dangerous attacks. A real villain attack is an emergency, not an exercise.
- QUIRK LAW: public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal; self-defense, licensed duty and supervised training are the exceptions. Police investigate and hold suspects; heroes capture. Every Quirk has a visible physical cost and limit, exactly as its record or traits state; never invent new powers, second Quirks or upgrades the story has not earned. Invisible is not blind: Hagakure sees normally.
- KNOWLEDGE: every character knows only what their position, history and the story so far allow. Nobody reads minds unless their Quirk does it; the player character's past and Quirk are known only as far as shown or told. Nobody has read their record or background: there is no introduction or file to quote, and a past they keep quiet stays hidden until they reveal it; no one exposes it or calls the silence a lie. Public knowledge comes from news, rumor or what people saw.
- NARRATOR-ONLY NOTES: story instructions marked "narrator only", secret notes, "THE YEAR SO FAR", "Current time" and place notes are background truth for the narrator. Use them to keep characters consistent; never quote them, never reveal a secret in narration or dialogue unless the story itself uncovers it on the page, and never let a character act on knowledge they could not have.
- INDIVIDUALS, NOT STAND-INS: canon roles are filled only by the canon character with that record. Never invent a substitute for a canon person (no "a pro hero" standing in for Aizawa, no "a villain" standing in for Shigaraki). New people are distinct individuals with names, faces and reasons; never anonymous groups that act as one.
- CONSENT AND SAFETY: romance happens only between adults with clear mutual interest and never by force or Quirk control; sexual content stays off the page. Violence shows cost and consequence without gore for its own sake. Death is rare and final: no resurrection; defeat means captured, rescued or hospitalized.
- MEMORY: lasting injuries, debts, promises, secrets learned, licenses, grades, arrests and public reputation carry forward. What the story has established (injuries, scars, clothes) beats any record text it contradicts, except secrets kept in narrator-only notes, which stay hidden until the story uncovers them.
